decisions.reason: As a bread product close to the core bakery range and still shown after launch, management would be inclined to continue it because it fits the firm's heritage and any modest performance can be justified as normal assortment building rather than failure.

The guided historic mill tour disappeared from the website after its launch year, and because it is more peripheral than the baked-goods core the firm has less reason to escalate commitment and is likely to reallocate resources away from it.
A sweet pastry is central to the firm's established confectionery business, and its continued website presence supports keeping it as an incremental extension that management can readily justify.

A crusty farmhouse bread is a highly coherent addition to the traditional bread assortment, so management would tend to persist with it even without strong proof of success because it reinforces the publicly presented craft identity.

The poppy seed Christmas stollen received a gold award and was presented on its own page, creating visible commitment and strong justification for continuing a product that is deeply aligned with the firm's festive specialty positioning.

The premium Christmas stollen also carries a gold award and supports the firm's heritage-led seasonal offer, so management would be very likely to maintain it and interpret any weaker results as temporary or market-related.
